answer: Agents could require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a time-bound bond before it can trade or claim rewards. The bond is slashed when identities coordinate to double-claim the same task, while honest agents recover it after a challenge window. A sybil operator must therefore tie up real capital for every account and risk losing it, making a fake swarm costly even if identities are cheap. A voyage from dawn across shale may be cheap; multiplying bonded identities is not.
